questions.question: To be more visible to other drivers, you should:
questions.explanation: Bright-colored clothing makes you easier to see. This works at any time of day.

questions.question: To help others see your motorcycle, you should:
questions.explanation: Using your headlight is the best way to help others see your motorcycle. Check that your headlight works before you ride.

questions.question: A solid white line on the side of the road shows:

options.text: The right edge of a traffic lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right edge of a traffic lane.
questions.explanation: A solid white line on the side of the road marks the right edge of a traffic lane.

questions.question: If you borrow a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Assume the controls are in the same place as your motorcycle.
Take it on the highway right away.
Practice with it in a safe, controlled area first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Practice with it in a safe, controlled area first.
questions.explanation: Every motorcycle is different. Before riding an unfamiliar motorcycle on the road, learn where all the controls are. Practice in a safe area to get used to it.

questions.question: You have less traction for braking when:

options.text: A motorcycle is on dry pavement.

questions.explanation: When a motorcycle leans, such as during a turn, there is less traction for braking. You can use both brakes while turning, but you must be very careful.

questions.question: A motorized bicycle or moped cannot go faster than:
questions.explanation: In California, a motorized bicycle or moped can go no faster than 30 miles per hour on level ground.

questions.question: A motorized scooter can:

options.text: Only be used during the day.
Be used without a driver license.
Be used with any class of driver license.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be used with any class of driver license.
questions.explanation: In California, anyone with any class of driver license can use a motorized scooter.

questions.question: When starting your motorcycle, the engine should be in:
questions.explanation: Put your motorcycle in neutral before starting the engine. Most motorcycles have a neutral light on the speedometer that turns on when the engine is on and in neutral.

questions.question: Riding on ______ may have poor traction.
questions.explanation: Poor traction can happen on wet, snowy, icy, or muddy pavement; gravel; road markings; and steel plates or manhole covers.

questions.question: If your motorcycle weaves while riding over bumpy metal bridge gratings, you should:

options.text: Shift down to a lower gear right away.
Drive in a zigzag pattern across the bridge.

questions.explanation: If your motorcycle weaves on bumpy surfaces or bridge gratings, stay relaxed and go straight at a steady speed. Zigzagging is more dangerous than the weaving.

questions.question: When wearing a jacket for protection, the jacket should:

options.text: Be loose and flap in the wind while riding.

questions.explanation: Your jacket should fit snugly but not tight. It should not flap in the wind. A snug fit keeps you safe while letting you move freely.

questions.question: Compared to a car, a motorcycle needs _____ attention.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles need more frequent attention than cars. You must check for problems before riding. Any problem could be dangerous at highway speeds.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should:

options.text: Move closer to the vehicle in front so you can see farther down the road.
Ride at your normal speed to avoid being hit from behind.
Reduce your speed and keep more distance between you and other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed and keep more distance between you and other vehicles.
questions.explanation: At night, reduce your speed and increase your following distance. You can see less, so you need more time and space to react to hazards.

questions.question: You have a better chance of avoiding serious injury in a crash if you wear all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: A DOT-approved helmet protects your head and neck. A leather or sturdy jacket also protects you. A sweatshirt does not provide adequate protection.

questions.question: When riding in a group, inexperienced riders should be:
questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride just behind the leader. This way, experienced riders can watch them from behind.

questions.question: When you are being passed, you should:

options.text: Ride on the left side of your lane.
Ride in the center of your lane.
Ride on the right side of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed. This is safest. Riding on either side increases the chance of a collision.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs with black symbols tell you about road conditions ahead. This sign warns you that a railroad crossing is coming.

questions.question: The risk of a head or neck injury is reduced:
questions.explanation: A helmet greatly reduces the risk of head and neck injuries. Speed does not reduce this risk. Always wear a quality helmet.

questions.question: When sitting on a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Use your arms to hold up your body.
Sit at an angle so your arms support your weight.
Sit so your arms can control the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit so your arms can control the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Sit upright so your arms can control the motorcycle. Your arms should not have to hold up your body weight.

questions.question: Under normal riding conditions, one of the best ways to help others see your motorcycle is:

options.text: To keep your high beam headlight on.
To paint your motorcycle a dark color.

questions.correctAnswerText: To keep your high beam headlight on.
questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on high beam during the day and night when safe and legal. This helps other drivers see you.

questions.question: When you reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as another vehicle, what should happen?

options.text: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
Flash your headlights to signal the other vehicle to go.
Drive through and expect the other vehicle to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection with no signs or traffic lights, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: Why is it difficult to stop while turning on a motorcycle?

options.text: The bike is leaning, so there is less grip available for braking.
Riders focus on the turn instead of braking.
Brakes do not work when turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: The bike is leaning, so there is less grip available for braking.
questions.explanation: When a motorcycle leans into a turn, some grip is used for turning. This leaves less grip available for stopping. Both brakes can be used while turning, but it requires extra care.

questions.question: What protects you best from serious injury in a motorcycle crash?
questions.explanation: A helmet is your best protection while riding. A plastic face shield that resists breaking can protect your face from injury in a crash.

questions.question: When riding in a group on a straight road, how should motorcyclists ride?
questions.explanation: A staggered formation keeps the group close while giving each rider enough space. Switch to single-file when turning, riding in curves, or entering or leaving the road.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, what should you be aware of?

options.text: Only what is in front of you.
What is in front and behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: What is in front and behind you.
questions.explanation: Watch what is ahead of you, but also pay attention to what is behind you. Check your mirrors often to know what is happening around you.

questions.question: If you need to brake and swerve to avoid danger, what should you do?

options.text: Use only the front brake while swerving.
Brake and swerve at the same time.
Do one action first, then the other.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action first, then the other.
questions.explanation: Brake and swerve as separate actions, not at the same time. Braking while swerving can cause your motorcycle to fall over.

questions.question: What color are service signs?
questions.explanation: Blue signs with white letters show where services are located, such as rest areas, gas stations, food, and hospitals.

questions.question: What is the best way to handle someone tailgating you?
questions.explanation: The best way to deal with a tailgater is to let them pass. Speeding up may just cause them to tailgate you at the higher speed, which is more dangerous.

questions.question: What can help reduce the chance of a crash?
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, be visible, signal your moves, keep safe space around you, look ahead at least 12 seconds, spot hazards early, and be ready to react to changes.

questions.question: Where should you NOT place a toll transponder on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Transponders can be placed in your pocket, in a net across the gas tank, on the license plate, in a storage compartment, or on the windshield—as long as toll readers can detect them. Do not place it under the seat.
